name: Stratum Executive Augment-Display Suit
description:
Designed for mid-to-senior corponation executives who wear their augmentation as credential, the Stratum Executive suit features chrome-display panels along the left lapel and cuff — thin strips of polished composite framing the visible edge of an implanted forearm or wrist augment, treating the chrome hardware as architectural detail rather than something to conceal. The fabric is a high-thread-count polysilk blend with a faint self-correcting weave that resists wrinkling for up to 72 hours under normal use. The jacket is cut with open channels at both inner forearms and a reinforced collar stay that accommodates a cervical BCI housing without bunching.

Stratum is an Ouroboros subsidiary, and the suit carries that lineage — conservative, intentional, designed to project competence rather than excess. It is the default formal uniform of the Ouroboros executive floor and appears frequently at inter-corponation negotiation sessions, Arcturus contractor review meetings, and Lazarus board presentations. The chrome-display panels have become a recognizable signifier in Tier 4 formal contexts: you have augments, you are not embarrassed by them, and you paid to have them framed correctly.
cultural_context: The chrome-display panel aesthetic emerged from Arcturus defense culture, where augmentation was always visible and functional. Stratum translated this into corporate formal language, normalizing the display of augment hardware in executive spaces. The suit has become a quiet power signal: executives who hide their chrome in cheaper suits are read as either ashamed of it or unable to afford the framing.
story_hooks: A mid-level Ouroboros analyst wears a counterfeit Stratum suit with fake chrome-display panels — no actual augments — to a Tier 4 networking event, and has to maintain the fiction all evening.
The chrome-display panels on a genuine Stratum suit are found to passively log nearby BCI handshake signatures — a Vantablack-adjacent data collection function buried in the composite material.
A character inherits this suit from a deceased corponation parent and has to decide whether to wear it to the estate proceedings — and what wearing it will signal to the assembled lawyers.

physical_description.visual_profile: A tailored single-breasted jacket with refined geometry and architectural intention. The silhouette reads corporate—structured shoulders, clean lines—but the chrome-display panels along the left lapel and cuffs create a deliberate visual interrupt: polished composite frames that showcase the visible edge of an augmented forearm or wrist implant as intentional hardware architecture rather than concealed enhancement. The effect is confident, calculated, and distinctly Tier 3-4 corporate.
physical_description.fit: Precision-tailored to corporate standard. Slim through the torso, allowing for layering or direct wear. Open channels run along both inner forearms to accommodate augment housings without binding. The reinforced collar stay is engineered to seat a cervical BCI without bunching or distortion. Cut to move with augmented limbs—fabric drapes around integrated hardware with engineered slack.
physical_description.primary_material: High-thread-count polysilk blend with self-correcting weave. The base is a refined synthetic-natural hybrid that resists wrinkling for up to 72 hours under normal corporate use. Chrome-display panels are polished composite strip-framing—not pure chrome, but composite engineered to catch light with architectural precision.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost liquid drape to the polysilk. The weave has a subtle luminescence under indoor lighting—the self-correcting technology creates a faint shimmer when the fabric moves. Chrome panels are mirror-polish, contrasting sharply with the matte finish of the surrounding textile. At close range, the seams along augment channels show reinforced stitching in tonal thread.
physical_description.color_scheme: Conservative corporate palette: charcoal grey, deep navy, or black as base. The chrome-display panels read as silver-mirror in standard lighting. Subtle tonal stitching (matching or one shade lighter than base). No pattern—the augment display *is* the pattern. Optional shirt layering in white, pearl grey, or deep teal.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap buttons disguised as traditional tailored buttons. The snaps are seamless—designed to release smoothly without catching on augment housing. Interior closure runs magnetic for reliability and silent operation.
distinctive_features: Chrome-display panels framing visible augment edges on left lapel and both cuffs
Open forearm channels engineered for augment accommodation
Reinforced collar stay designed to seat cervical BCI housing without bunching
Self-correcting polysilk weave resists wrinkling for 72 hours
Magnetic snap closures disguised as tailored buttons
Architectural precision in proportions—every measurement intentional
Interior augment-access channels with reinforced stitching
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 formal wear. The price point is Tier 3 accessibility but the confidence it projects signals Tier 2-3 executive positioning. Wearing this suit means you can afford to display your augments correctly.
physical_description.cultural_context: The Stratum Executive suit is the default formal uniform of Ouroboros executive floors and appears at inter-corponation negotiation sessions, Arcturus contractor reviews, and Lazarus board presentations. The chrome-display aesthetic originated in Arcturus defense culture (where augmentation is always visible and functional) and was translated into corporate formal language by Stratum Clothiers. Wearing this suit signals: augmented, unashamed, and competent enough to afford the framing. In Tier 4 formal contexts, executives who hide their chrome in cheaper suits are read as either embarrassed or unable to afford the intentional display.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on first wear, remaining crisp for 72 hours due to self-correcting weave. With regular care, shows minimal wrinkling or wear at stress points. Chrome panels maintain mirror-polish under normal maintenance. The augment channels show no visible strain or fraying—engineered for durability. Over extended use, the fabric develops a subtle patina, the weave settles into the body's contours, and the chrome panels may require occasional re-polish, but the suit maintains executive presentation indefinitely.

image_prompt: A sleek corporate executive in a charcoal Stratum Executive Augment-Display suit stands against a darkened floor-to-ceiling window overlooking the GLMZ skyline at dusk. Left arm extended to show the polished chrome-display panel framing a visible forearm implant housing—the chrome catches the ambient light from downtown corporate towers. The jacket is tailored with precise geometry, magnetic buttons catching highlights. Interior BCI cervical housing visible at the collar, framed by reinforced stay without bunching. The polysilk blend has subtle luminescence. Moody gel lighting: cool blue and steel grey. The augment is displayed as architectural credential, not concealment. Shot from a three-quarter angle emphasizing the left lapel chrome framing. Dark minimal background with subtle corpo-tower bokeh. --ar 2:3 --v 6
